transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Ellen Park (NovaEscalate CTO), Ravi Menon (Lead ML Eng), Sofia Alvarez (PM), Tom Briggs (Infra)

Summary: quick POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and integration plan. Focus on SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, tool/function calling, and structured output. Discussed hosted vs dedicated, security needs (SOC2, SSO), and a 3-4 week pilot timeline.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate you taking the time. i'm maya from redwood, i'm the AE on this. quick intros?
00:08 Ellen: hey maya, ellen here, cto at novaescalate. we've got ravi, sofia and tom on as well.
00:13 Ravi: hi all.
00:15 Maya: awesome, jordan and lena are our SEs, jordan will drive technical stuff today. goal is to get to a scoped poc next steps and baseline success criteria.
00:25 Jordan: yeah thanks. maybe quick agenda — 1) what are you trying to validate in the poc, 2) workload profile and sizing, 3) integration approach (sdks / openai-compat endpoints), 4) benchmarks & timeline, 5) next steps. sound good?
00:38 Ellen: sounds good. our big picture — we want an assistant that augments our customer support workflow and internal triage. main concerns are p99 latency, cost per ticket, and data residency (europe first).
00:52 Sofia: also want structured output (JSON) back from the model for ticket fields and routing, and ability to call internal tools for enrichment.
01:00 Jordan: cool, two quick clarifications — structured output can be done via constrained generation or function/tool calling. redwood supports both; function calls are available via our openai-compatible endpoints and SDKs.
01:15 Ravi: openai-compatible endpoints? can you elaborate — we run an adapter to their existing codebase so minimal changes.
01:21 Jordan: yup, we expose an OpenAI-compatible REST surface (POST /v1/chat/completions style) plus native SDKs for node/python. function calling uses the same call pattern but a function schema is included, and our runtime will return a structured payload or trigger call hooks depending on config.
01:36 Tom: any caveats on streaming + function calling? we rely on streaming to update UI progressively.
01:42 Lena: streaming works, but when using function calling you can get an intermediate function call object then a final structured response. there are some small edge cases around chunked function payloads — i've seen transcribe as kv cache — sorry, k v cache — where partials arrive, but we can walk through a sample.
01:58 Maya: let's jump into success criteria — what are your must-haves for the poc?
02:03 Ellen: musts: p99 inference latency under 400ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens), end-to-end <600ms including network for europe region; structured JSON correctness > 95% on our evaluation set; no customer data leaves eu for the test; and integration via minimal code changes (openai-compat).
02:24 Jordan: noted. for the latency numbers, are you planning to use hosted (redwood api) or dedicated capacity?
02:31 Ellen: preference for hosted initially for speed of setup but if we hit inconsistent latency or need guaranteed throughput we'll look at dedicated.
02:39 Ravi: also want to run a cost projection: estimate tokens per ticket and qps during peak (we expect 10 qps sustained, 40 qps bursts). typical prompt sizes: 350 tokens in, expected 120 tokens out.
02:55 Jordan: good, that's actionable. for sizing we usually convert to tokens/sec and check concurrency. with 10 qps and 470 tokens roundtrip that's about 4.7k tokens/sec. on a modern 80GB quantized model on a single GPU we can reach x throughput — (note: model choice matters).
03:14 Maya: can we capture the model family you plan to test? any preference for open foundation models vs a hosted finetuned model?
03:22 Ravi: we prefer an open model, something with instruction tuning. cost sensitivity is high. also we may run a smaller test with a finetuned in-house model later.
03:31 Jordan: makes sense. we'll plan to propose a curated open model from our catalog with latency profiles.
03:36 Sofia: benchmarks — what will you run during the poc and how long does it take?
03:40 Lena: typically we run two phases: functional correctness (structured output tests using your eval set) and performance benchmarks (qps, p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm cache). we run synthetic traffic + replayed samples. benchmark run usually takes a day to provision and run, then a day to analyze.
03:53 Jordan: and we'll include KV/prefix caching on the prompts where it makes sense — that can reduce token compute by up to 30% on repeat flows.
04:00 Tom: on security, we need SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), and audit logs. also need option for private deployment later — how does redwood handle that?
04:10 Maya: we have a Private option (VPC or on-prem) — customers who need strict controls can use a private control plane and customer-managed keys. for the poc we can provision hosted but with EU region and retention policies set to not store logs, and provide audit logs for the run. we'll share SOC2 docs and SAML integration guide.
04:27 Ravi: great. timeline? we want something within december — is 3 weeks realistic?
04:31 Jordan: timeline depends on receiving your eval set and traffic profile. assuming we get assets this week, typical timeline: week 1 — integration + smoke tests, week 2 — benchmark runs and iterate on prompt templates, week 3 — final analysis and handoff. so 2-3 weeks is doable.
04:50 Sofia: decision criteria for success — can we record them: 1) p99 < 400ms (in region), 2) structured extraction accuracy >95% on eval set, 3) integration effort < 3 dev days using openai-compat sdk, 4) cost estimate within budget (TBD).
05:08 Maya: captured. we'll formalize in the poc doc.
05:12 Ellen: about integration — do you have sample SDK code for function calling and structured responses? our front-end is react/node, back end python.
05:20 Jordan: yes. we'll share a node + python example that mirrors OpenAI function calling. sample payload will include functions schema and we show how the sdk returns a parsed json. also we'll include streaming + partial function events example.
05:35 Ravi: how invasive is the change? i.e., our current code calls openai chat completions, can you be drop-in?
05:40 Lena: mostly drop-in — endpoints are compatible but there are extra headers for tenant keys. we also have client libraries with a 1-2 line swap example. in some edge cases where you use advanced parameters (e.g., custom batching, custom kv cache controls) you'll need a few lines, but it shouldn't be more than a day.
05:59 Tom: for benchmarking, will you provide test keys for hosted instances or do we test on dedicated?
06:04 Jordan: for the poc we typically provision a temporary hosted key in EU region. if you prefer dedicated we can spin up reserved capacity but that takes longer. the hosted benchmark is usually sufficient to validate latency/cost for your traffic profile.
06:19 Ravi: any gotchas on telemetry and observability? we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency.
06:25 Lena: we expose per-request traces in the console and we can give you a sample dashboard; token-level cost breakouts are available as well. we'll include traces in the benchmark output so you can correlate slow tails with model variants or network hops.
06:40 Sofia: function calling — can the function call trigger our internal enrichment service? i.e., model returns function call then redwood invokes our webhook?
06:46 Jordan: yes, you can configure function hooks; we support synchronous function responses or preflight webhooks. you'll provide a function schema + URL and we can run the enrichment as part of the pipeline. security note: webhook endpoints should be on your side in EU and we recommend mTLS for sensitive flows.
07:00 Ellen: good. on structured output accuracy — how do you measure it?
07:03 Lena: we run your eval set (labeled tickets) and measure exact match on fields plus fuzzy match for free-text fields; we'll produce a per-field precision/recall report. we'll also run a human-in-the-loop pass for ambiguous ones.
07:15 Ravi: benchmarks for throughput — you mentioned model choice matters. can you provide a few model profiles and expected p99 numbers for our payload size?
07:23 Jordan: yes we'll include 3 candidate models in the poc doc: a smaller faster one (good latency, lower quality), a mid-tier instruction tuned model (balanced), and a heavier high-quality model (slower, more costly). we'll give p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens estimates from our catalog.
07:40 Maya: let's recap actions and timeline. if novaescalate can send the eval set and traffic profile by monday (2026-12-14) we can start integration that week and aim to have benchmarks by 2026-12-18. final report and decision brief by 2026-12-22. does that work?
07:57 Ellen: yes monday is fine.
08:00 Sofia: one more thing — we might want event-level structured outputs for routing (JSON with priority, queue, suggested tags). ensure the schema is part of the eval.
08:11 Jordan: noted. please include schema and examples in the eval bundle.
08:16 Maya: anything else on security or compliance?
08:19 Tom: just retention — we need logs wiped after 30 days for the poc and proof of EU-only storage.
08:25 Maya: we'll set retention policies accordingly and provide logs proving residency.
08:29 Ellen: ok great. thanks, this was useful.
08:33 Maya: thanks everyone. we'll send the poc plan and pricing.

End of call.

Notes: conversation had typical transcript artifacts — slight word swaps and filler. references to kv cache sometimes transcribed as "k v cache".

Attachments referenced: poc-plan-deck.pdf (to be shared), sdk-samples repo link (to be shared), security-pack.zip (SOC2 + SAML guide).

POC Success criteria (captured):
- p99 inference latency < 400ms in EU region (end-to-end <600ms)
- Structured extraction accuracy >= 95% on provided eval set
- Integration effort < 3 developer days using OpenAI-compatible SDK/endpoint
- Cost estimate within customer budget (TBD)

Benchmarks to run:
- Functional accuracy run on eval set (2k labeled tickets sample)
- Synthetic throughput run: 10 qps sustained with 40 qps bursts, prompt sizes ~350 tokens in / 120 tokens out
- Cold vs warm cache runs to quantify caching gains

Timeline:
- 2026-12-14: NovaEscalate to provide eval set, traffic profile, schema
- 2026-12-15: Redwood to provision hosted test key in EU region and share SDK samples
- 2026-12-16 to 2026-12-17: benchmark runs and initial analysis
- 2026-12-18: benchmark results shared
- 2026-12-22: final report and decision brief
